messages:
mike: Quick spike — big qdrep files and noisy kernels when we capture full runs. Thinking of splitting captures into small windows + randomized sampling to reduce noise from prefix warmup. any obvious pitfalls?
jess: agreed, single long capture mixes warmup + steady state. I'd do short windows around interesting NVTX regions instead of full-process capture.
Samir: +1. Also try `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` and `--sample=cpu` for a lighter-weight view.
mike: sample=cpu good call. what about duration? our seqs are 1.2s average but tails exist.
tara: use `--duration=10s` for smoke then `--duration=30s` for a stable window. but more important: use capture-range with NVTX brackets so we only record actual infer sections: `--capture-range=nvtx:inference_start,inference_end`.
jess: if you can't instrument NVTX for every microcase, another trick is multiple randomized short captures: run N traces with `--duration=5s` and jitter start time. then aggregate hotspots across runs. reduces large-file overhead.
mike: that sounds promising. how do we aggregate? people just eyeball with timeline?
samir: small script: run traces in a loop, extract kernel names from `nsys stats` or use `nsys export --format=sqlite` and query kernel table; then count occurrences/medians. cheap way: `nsys stats -f cuda api.qdrep` and parse top kernels.
jess: also watch out for OSRT noise — sometimes OSRT sampling shows up as many small tasks. If you include `osrt` in trace, filter by thread name or PID. `--trace=cuda,nvtx` might be enough for kernel hotspots.
mike: we need kv-cache heat/evict spikes; will NVTX brackets cover that?
tara: instrument cache ops: emit `NVTX_MARKER` around `kv_get`/`kv_evict` so you can correlate kernel bursts with cache events. avoid tracing every tiny op — bracket the heavier ops only.
mike: paste of my quick run: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=12s -o probe1` produced a 1.2GB qdrep in 12s. repeated 10x is painful.
jess: yep that's why short randomized runs win. for 5s runs you should get ~300MB each; then discard noisy ones.
sys-bot: tip: `nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=nvtx:inference_start --capture-range-end=nvtx:inference_end` maps to bracketed NVTX ranges.
samir: if qdrep size still huge, use `--trace=cuda,nvtx -w true` (wait/quiet mode) or `--output` compression flags depending on version. also `nsys` 2023+ supports `--sample=none` and relying on CUDA activity only.
mike: good. any heuristics for number of randomized runs? 20? 5?
tara: depends on variance. start with 10-20 short windows, compute median kernel time per kernel across runs. kernels that persist in median are real hotspots.
jess: for batching heuristics test: run varied batch sizes across randomized captures, then aggregate the KV-prefetch/evict markers to see when eviction correlates with latency spikes.
mike: thanks — I'll add NVTX around kv ops, do 12 runs of 5s with jitter, parse `nsys stats` and report back.
samir: if you want I can toss together the sqlite -> csv query to find median durations by kernel name.
mike: please do, that'll save time. tagging you offline. :thumbsup:
